title: Two-Ball Dribbling Ladder
description: Dribble two balls together through a cone ladder, moving from stationary work to forward movement to build both hands, rhythm and coordination.

content.objective: Build strong, controlled two-handed dribbling with the head up, moving through a cone ladder at increasing speed.
content.setup: Four cones in a line about two metres apart on the court. Players line up at one end with two balls, one behind another and start at intervals.
instructions: Stationary: dribble both balls at the same time at waist height for 20 seconds.
Alternate the balls: one high, one low, then swap.
Walk forward through the cone ladder while dribbling both balls, the lead ball on the outside of each cone.
Jog through the ladder, then finish with both balls dribbled behind the back once at every cone.
Rest, then repeat with the opposite ball leading.
coachingPoints: Eyes up: look at the coach or a target at the end of the line.
Pound the ball with fingertips, not the palm.
Keep the dribble low when moving and high when stationary.
Relax the shoulders and keep a steady rhythm.
commonMistakes: Looking at the balls the whole time.
Dribbling with the palm instead of fingertips.
Going too fast and losing control.
content.safety: Keep the line clear of other players and pick up loose balls immediately to avoid slipping.
progressions: Add a variation such as crossover or between-the-legs at every cone.
regressions: Use one ball in the strong hand and one in the weak hand alternately.
variations: Two players race in adjoining lanes without losing control.
